t.E330.agn: In 1973 JECFA set the group ADI for citric acid and its calcium, potassium, sodium and ammonium salts as 'not limited'. JECFA reported that frequent or high intake of citric acid may cause dental erosion and local irritation because of its low pH.
t.E330.body: Citric acid and citrates are normal intermediates of the tricarboxylic acid (Krebs) cycle, which produces energy in the body.
t.E330.eff.0.t: May cause erosion of tooth enamel and irritation in the mouth because of its low pH
t.E330.found.0: May be used in many foods in the EU at quantum satis (as much as needed)
t.E330.found.1: Infant formulae and complementary foods for infants (in the EU only under limited conditions such as pH adjustment)
t.E330.prod: Mostly produced by fermentation of sugars with the mould Aspergillus niger (sometimes with Candida yeast).
t.E330.regx.0: Group ADI 'not limited' (citric acid and its salts).
t.E330.regx.1: Group I additive; generally permitted at quantum satis (as much as needed).
t.E330.summary: An acid found naturally in citrus fruits such as lemons and oranges; today it is mostly produced by fermentation of sugar or starch with mould. It gives a sour taste, regulates acidity and supports antioxidants; it is one of the most widely used additives in drinks, confectionery, jams and canned foods.
t.E330.what: An acidity regulator that gives food sourness, adjusts pH and supports the effect of antioxidants.
